_about: One sentence per forecast source, for hover and tap tooltips on both sites. Written by projects-97, read by projects-5a. Keys match live/common.py LIVE_MODELS short names plus Open-Meteo model ids.

blend.name: DK Wind Live forecast
blend.text: Four weather models (ECMWF IFS, ECMWF AIFS, DMI HARMONIE, DWD ICON-EU) each turned into megawatts by their own trained power model, then averaged with equal weight.

energinet.name: Energinet (bias-corrected)
energinet.text: The Danish grid operator's own day-ahead wind forecast, rescaled by its actual-to-forecast ratio over the previous 60 days, because its DK1 offshore forecast covers only part of the fleet.

energinet_raw.name: Energinet (as published)
energinet_raw.text: The Danish grid operator's own day-ahead wind forecast as published; its DK1 offshore part is capped near 1,000 MW while the fleet now peaks near 2,000 MW.

ifs.name: ECMWF IFS
ifs.text: The European weather centre's main physics model, run on a global grid of about 25 km in this archive; the reference most weather desks start from.

ifs_9km.name: ECMWF IFS 9 km
ifs_9km.text: The same European physics model at its native 9 km resolution.

aifs.name: ECMWF AIFS (AI)
aifs.text: The European weather centre's AI model, a neural network trained on decades of reconstructed past weather; fast and accurate on average, but smooth, so it tends to soften the strongest winds.

harmonie.name: DMI HARMONIE
harmonie.text: The Danish Meteorological Institute's own high-resolution model, a grid of about 2 km over Northern Europe, run several times a day.

knmi.name: KNMI HARMONIE
knmi.text: The Dutch weather service's version of the same HARMONIE model, about 5.5 km grid, covering Denmark from the south-west.

icon.name: DWD ICON-EU
icon.text: The German weather service's European model, about 7 km grid; best at real Danish anemometers in the history study.

icon_d2.name: DWD ICON-D2
icon_d2.text: The German weather service's 2 km model for Germany and its neighbours, which reaches only two days ahead.

icon_global.name: DWD ICON global
icon_global.text: The German weather service's global model, about 11 km grid.

gfs.name: NOAA GFS
gfs.text: The United States' global physics model, about 25 km grid, free and widely used.

graphcast.name: Google GraphCast (AI)
graphcast.text: Google DeepMind's AI weather model, here started from the American GFS analysis.

ukmo.name: UK Met Office
ukmo.text: The British weather service's global model, about 10 km grid; only 10 m wind is archived, so it is scored at 10 m.

ukmo_2km.name: UK Met Office 2 km
ukmo_2km.text: The British weather service's 2 km model for the UK and the North Sea.

metno.name: MET Norway Nordic
metno.text: The Norwegian weather service's 1 km Nordic model, corrected with thousands of local observations.

gem.name: Canada GEM
gem.text: Environment Canada's global model, about 15 km grid.

jma.name: Japan JMA
jma.text: The Japan Meteorological Agency's global model, about 55 km grid over Europe, the coarsest in the field.

cma.name: China CMA GRAPES
cma.text: The China Meteorological Administration's global model, about 15 km grid.

bom.name: Australia BOM ACCESS
bom.text: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology global model, about 15 km grid.

arpege.name: Meteo-France ARPEGE
arpege.text: The French weather service's model, finest over Europe at about 10 km.

era5.name: ERA5
era5.text: ECMWF's reconstruction of past weather: a weather model fed every available observation, giving an hourly map of the atmosphere on a 31 km grid back to 1940; the answer key for maps, but smooth.

accuracy.name: Accuracy
accuracy.text: 100% minus the day's total forecast error divided by the day's total output, over the four zones (DK1 and DK2, offshore and onshore); 100% would be perfect.

band.name: 80% band
band.text: The range that should contain the real output in 8 hours out of 10; it widens when the four weather models disagree and when more wind is forecast.
